description: Hexactra MCP server (hexactra-mcp): operate the user's browser through the control plane /v1 API.
instructions: These tools operate a real Chrome browser, and the computer it runs on, on behalf of the user who owns them; it is signed in to their accounts. Work like a person at the machine. Start with browser_navigate, then browser_elements (CSS selectors) and browser_click / browser_type. When the page structure does not help (canvas, custom widgets, unlabeled icons), look at it: browser_screenshot with marks=true numbers the interactive elements and gives their boxes, and browser_click_at / browser_mouse / browser_drag / browser_scroll_at / browser_type_keys / browser_key act by position with trusted input. browser_evaluate runs any JavaScript in the page. For anything outside the page (native dialogs, file pickers, other windows) use the browser_desktop_* tools on the whole screen. When the person themself is needed (a CAPTCHA puzzle, a code sent to their phone, a passkey), call browser_request_human; browser actions pause while it is open. A secret the person gives (input=secret) is never shown to you: type it with browser_type_secret.
name: hexactra

tools.description: Pause and ask the user to do something only a person should do, or a question only they can answer: solve a CAPTCHA, enter a one-time code, approve a passkey, sign in, confirm a purchase, pick from options. The user is reached on their configured channels (chat, email link, ...). With wait=true (default) this returns the outcome and the person's answer: `value` for text, choice (the option id), number (a decimal string) and confirm (`approve` or `deny`), `values` (option ids) for multi_choice. Use input=secret for one-time codes and passwords: the answer is never returned (`value_withheld`); type it into the page with browser_type_secret and the handoff_id. Use input=takeover when the person must operate the browser themselves.

choices.description: Options for choice and multi_choice: a string (used as id and label) or {id, label, description}.

constraints.description: Bounds on the answer; only those that apply to the input are allowed.

pattern.description: text: regex the whole answer must match

input.description: none: the person acts in the browser and marks it done. takeover: the person operates the browser, then marks it done. confirm: approve or deny.

prompt.description: What the person should do, in plain words.

risk.description: confirm: how risky approving is (default high)

tools.name: browser_request_human

tools.description: Check (and optionally wait for) a request created by browser_request_human with wait=false.
tools.name: browser_handoff_status
